chat.afterOutput: Briefly interpret the output. Only if my goal is still open: next command.

panel.title: AI assistant
panel.unsupportedTab: The assistant works with SSH, PowerShell and CMD tabs.
panel.noProvider: No AI provider has been set up yet.
panel.setupInMain: Set up a provider in the main window.
panel.hint1: Say what you want to achieve, e.g. “I want to restart the pods in the monitoring namespace.” The assistant suggests the matching command; Type in puts it on the input line. After you press Enter, it reads the output, summarizes it in one sentence and only continues while your goal is still open.
panel.hint2: Explanations only on request (“explain…”). The last terminal lines go to <provider/> along with your question. Commands reach the input line only with Type in and run only when you press Enter.
panel.inserted: Written to the input line, not executed
panel.awaiting: Check the command and press Enter in the terminal.
panel.awaitingAuto: The assistant then reads the output and briefly interprets it.
panel.outputReady: Output of “{{command}}” is ready and will go along with your next question.
panel.inputPlaceholder: Question about the terminal… (Enter sends, Shift+Enter new line)

settings.title: AI providers
settings.intro: API keys are stored encrypted in the vault and only used by the Shellherd main process. What you ask the assistant goes to the selected provider along with the terminal excerpt.
settings.invalid: Check the name, model and URL (with https:// or http://).
settings.azureEndpointMissing: For Azure you need the endpoint of the resource.
settings.deploymentHint: e.g. the small chat model “minichat” or gpt-4o-mini.
settings.endpointHint: Project or resource URL from the Foundry portal, e.g. https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>. Shellherd finds the right call path itself.
settings.apiVersionHint: Usually leave empty. Only applies to the /models and /openai/deployments paths.
